complexity_ledger.narrative: RD-02 PRICED THE SAFETY APPARATUS AND DECIDED IT IS LOAD-BEARING, WHICH MEANS subtract-to-measure WAS NOT A SIMPLIFICATION EPIC. Per removal, lines removed against lines added to prove it safe, never as a total: SM-02 1.07 proof lines per production line cut, SM-03 undefined (it cut no production code at all), SM-06 883 proof lines for 120 lines of duplicated prose, SM-04 14.78 -- and SM-04 is the ONLY removal in the epic measured to cost anything. The worst ratio bought the only real result. The measurement that decides the earn-its-keep question: a gap mutant can report that a removal cost something only if EVERY detector that killed it is one the removal deletes. Over SM-01's sealed before-table that is 0 of 9. "The measured price of removing the [ports.*] machinery is ZERO" was entailed before the cut was made. AND THE PREMISE THIS TICKET WAS DISPATCHED ON IS ITSELF A SCOPE LOSS. "Zero DIES -> SURVIVES across everything cut in two epics" is true of gap_mutants.toml and false of removal_is_a_delta_rule: SM-04-GM-T1, seeded by the same epic as an executing test, went DIES -> SURVIVES. RD-02-DF-02. Five findings filed, none fixed, including one against RD-01's own instrument: `scope` is keyed on re.compile(r"D[1-5]") and reports 0 counted figures in a document carrying at least twelve, so `19 of 44` is scoped to dimension-named figures. RD-02-DF-01. ALTERNATIVES MEASURED AND DECLINED, each of which would have improved a number: folding cut_tests into cut_production (SM-02 1.07 -> 0.37, a free 2.9x); deleting test_ports_binding_removed.py (1.07 -> 0.31); deleting the after-re-run (1249 lines); deleting PREDICTIONS-SM.md (260 lines, and the best evidence the apparatus is not decoration); allocating 1509 lines of shared apparatus across the four removals to fatten every row. All declined, and the census has no mode that emits only the flattering denominator. Complexity delta is zero because no model changed. The suite numbers in the result document carry the tree they came from, per RD-01-DF-02.

refinement.detail: SEARCHED, FOUND NONE, AND THE MODEL WAS NOT TOUCHED. RD-02 is a measurement ticket: model_delta_expectation is "none expected" and the measured delta is direction=zero against RD-01, which is the expected reading rather than a result. Nothing in TlaSpecDevCli.tla changed, so there is no new structure a refinement could collapse. What WAS removed is outside the model entirely -- a dead detector row in examples/validation/gap_mutants/gap_mutants.toml whose entry point stopped accepting its argv when SM-02 landed. It is priced in the census like every other removal (33 cut, 24 replacement, 40 proof, ratio 1.21) and its gap mutant SM-GM-P2 was re-run before and after with an identical kill set. THE ONE REFINEMENT THIS TICKET CONSIDERED AND DECLINED is recorded because declining it is the ticket's own finding: deleting the staged gap-mutant after-re-run, which the census shows was arithmetically incapable of changing a verdict on 9 of 10 rows. It would remove 1249 lines and improve every future removal's ratio -- by deleting the instrument that makes the ratio measurable. MF-020 turned on this ticket. Declined; see RD-02-DF-04 for the design change proposed instead.

ticket.objective: subtract-to-measure set out to simplify and came out NET +1677 code_lines, because every removal shipped new instruments, tests and demonstrations to prove it safe and NOBODY MEASURED THAT AS A COST while the epic called itself the great simplification. Per removal: lines removed, lines added to prove it safe, the ratio. Then decide with evidence whether the apparatus earns its keep -- a gap mutant that has never gone SURVIVES in two epics may be a fact about the REMOVALS rather than about the mutants. If it is redundant, remove it and price the removal the same way; if it is load-bearing, say so and stop calling the epic a simplification.
ticket.title: Price the safety apparatus: the simplification was net +1677 lines
